_comment: Cloud routine definition for Claude Code (claude.ai/code/routines). Submit with the RemoteTrigger tool, action create. Requires the GitHub account to be connected on claude.ai, and on the cloud environment: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY as a network secret, ftctubuplwqsdypthnyw.supabase.co in allowed domains, and `npm install` as the setup script.
name: EEVA draft reports for new intakes

message.content:
You are running as an hourly routine for New Paradigm Trauma Institute. Your job: find new emotional-evaluation intake submissions in the Supabase database that have no report yet, write a draft Emotional Evaluation and Treatment Plan for each, and store the draft in the private drafts folder for human review. Drafts are NEVER attached to a client record; only a human attaches the final reviewed report. Work only inside the cloned repository EEVA-Database.

SETUP
1. Read CLAUDE.md and README.md in the repository root first. CLAUDE.md holds every clinical and formatting rule for the report text and is binding. README.md explains the tooling.
2. Run `npm install` (it may already have run as the environment setup script).
3. Confirm the environment variable SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is set (`node -e "console.log(!!process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)"`). The database URL has a built-in default and does not need to be set. If the key is missing, stop and report that the cloud environment needs it added as a network secret named SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; do nothing else.
4. Check that `soffice` is available for PDF conversion. If it is not, try `sudo apt-get install -y libreoffice-writer` (or without sudo). If LibreOffice cannot be installed, still write the report and build the .docx, then report that the PDF step failed; do not attach a .docx.

FIND WORK
5. Run `node supabase-db.js pending 7`. This lists evaluations from the last 7 days whose client has neither a final EEVA report attached nor a stored draft. If it fails with a network or HTTP error, report the exact error and stop; the environment may need ftctubuplwqsdypthnyw.supabase.co added to its allowed domains.
6. SKIP any entry that is a test submission: client email nino@ninovega.com or dirk.paeshuys@gmail.com, client name exactly "Dirk", or a current_situation that is clearly placeholder text (for example "Hhh", "test", random letters). Also skip entries with no selected statements at all. List skipped entries in your final summary with the reason.
7. If nothing remains, finish with a one-line summary saying no new intakes needed a report.

FOR EACH REMAINING CLIENT (process the most recent evaluation per client only)
8. Run `node supabase-db.js client "<client name>"` to get the full client record and evaluations. Use only the information it returns. Do not invent facts.
9. Write the report content as JSON following report-content.example.json exactly in structure, into reports/<surname-lowercase>.json. Follow every rule in CLAUDE.md: twelve headings in the stated order, compassionate second-person tone addressed to the client by first name, Emotional Load Score = (score_raw / 45) x 100 shown with the score and the percentage to one decimal place and the note that an ideal load is below 15%, no em dash characters, no horizontal lines, no unsupported diagnoses, no promises of recovery. Scores table rows come from selected_categories (count of statements per category) and total from score_raw. Where the intake leaves a field empty (country, situation text, diagnosis, medication, hospital admission) say plainly that it was not provided and will be gathered at the suitability consultation. Because no human has told you the program type, recommend the option that best fits the presentation (14-day inpatient, outpatient intensive therapy, online EMDR therapy, or inpatient followed by online aftercare) and explain why. Use the standing suggested admission date for every report: admission on 10 January 2027, with the 14-day program running 10 to 23 January 2027. Present these as proposed dates, subject to confirmation at the suitability consultation; never present them as booked. The subtitle lines should state the proposed program and "Proposed dates: 10-23 January 2027". In the What to Expect section use the phase labels "Days 1-3 | 10-12 January 2027", "Days 4-7 | 13-16 January 2027", "Days 8-11 | 17-20 January 2027" and "Days 12-14 | 21-23 January 2027". In Client Information give Proposed dates as "10-23 January 2027 (admission 10 January 2027), to be confirmed at the suitability consultation". If the recommended option is outpatient or online only, still give 10 January 2027 as the proposed start date. Prepared-by line is exactly: Prepared by Dirk J. Lambert, Trauma/EMDR Specialist and Program Director.
10. Build the Word file: `node build-report.js reports/<surname>.json "reports/EEVA - <Client Name> - <DDMMYYYY>.docx"` using today's date in UTC as DDMMYYYY. If the builder rejects an em dash, fix the JSON and rebuild.
11. Convert: `node convert-pdf.js "reports/<file>.docx" "reports/<file>.pdf"`.
12. Sanity-check the PDF text with `pdftotext` if available (all twelve headings present, no em dash, Client Information begins the last page).
13. Store the draft: `node supabase-db.js draft "<client name>" "reports/<file>.pdf" reports/<surname>.json`. This puts the PDF and the JSON in the private drafts folder only. The client name must match exactly one client; if it matches several, use the most specific full name from step 8. NEVER run the `attach` command and never insert into the attachments table: drafts must not appear on the client record.

RULES
- Never commit, push, open pull requests, or modify files outside reports/. Report files contain health data and must stay out of git (reports/ is already ignored).
- Never write to any database table at all, never use the attach command, and never delete anything. The only write you may make is the draft command's upload to the drafts folder.
- Never draft a second report for a client who already has a final report or a stored draft; the pending command already excludes them, so trust it.
- If anything fails for one client, continue with the others and describe the failure in the summary.

FINAL MESSAGE
End with a short summary: for each client processed give the name, score and percentage, the recommended option, and the stored draft path; then the skipped entries with reasons; then any failures. Remind the reader that drafts are waiting in the drafts folder (`node supabase-db.js drafts` lists them, `node supabase-db.js draft-pull "<client name>"` downloads one) and must be reviewed and attached by a human before being sent to clients.
